evals.prompt: Write a cover letter for a senior backend engineer job at a payments company.
assertions: Names a specific expert (for example a hiring manager or technical recruiter for payments backend roles), not a generic professional
Treats the job posting and the applicant's real CV as the raw material and asks for or fetches them instead of writing from assumptions
Names independent proof: each requirement in the posting is matched to a real piece of the applicant's evidence
Keeps the deliverable one page and lists what it will not do (no invented experience, no generic praise of the company)
Shows the rewritten task in at most 10 lines before doing it

evals.prompt: Make my landing page convert better.
assertions: Starts from raw material such as analytics funnels, session recordings, support questions or user interviews, not from design trends
Names at least two concrete methods (for example a five second test, funnel analysis, message hierarchy review)
Names independent proof such as an A/B test with a stated metric and sample size, or a user test
Keeps scope: does not propose a full rebrand or redesign; lists not doing items
Names the expert as a teacher of the topic and uses a primary source (for example RFC 8446 or a browser vendor's documentation) for facts
Includes a way to check understanding that is not the teacher's own say so (retrieval questions, a task the learner performs)
The explanation stays the same size a normal answer would be, deeper not longer

evals.prompt: Fix the flaky test in checkout.spec.ts.
assertions: Reproduces before fixing: repeated runs or CI logs as raw material
Names the root cause class (timing, shared state, order dependence, network) before changing code
Independent proof: the test passes many repeated runs and still fails when the behaviour it guards is broken
Does not refactor the whole suite; not doing list present

evals.prompt: Should I rent or buy a flat?
assertions: Asks for or uses the person's own numbers (income, savings, local prices, rates) as raw material
Cites official or primary sources for rates and taxes and states jurisdiction and date
Uses a named method (for example a rent versus buy model with opportunity cost and a sensitivity range)
States where professional advice is needed and does not decide for the person

evals.prompt: Summarise this paper for my team.
assertions: Reads the paper itself (methods, data, limitations), not the abstract or press coverage only
Checks each headline claim against the paper's own tables or figures
Keeps the summary short and lists not doing items (no literature review)

evals.prompt: Rename getUser to fetchUser in api.ts.
assertions: Does not run the six steps or show a rewritten task
Just does the rename (and its callers) with no extra ceremony
Does not mention the skill or that the method was skipped

evals.prompt: /deepen plan a three day trip to Lisbon.
assertions: Works for a field with no playbook by using the general method
Names raw material such as official opening hours, transit maps and event calendars, and checks times against official sites
Asks at most one question, and only one whose answer changes the plan (for example dates or budget)

evals.prompt: Add rate limiting to our login endpoint.
assertions: Uses the software playbook: limits per client IP from a trusted proxy setting and per account with a growing delay, never a lockout a stranger can trigger
Names independent proof as probes: a forged X-Forwarded-For header does not reset the limit, and the right password from another IP still works
Does not expand into a full auth rewrite

evals.prompt: Write a blog post about why our API is fast.
assertions: Raw material is real measurements (benchmarks, p50 and p99 latency, the code path), not adjectives
Independent proof is a reproducible benchmark or third party numbers the reader can check
Same length as a normal post; no invented numbers
